description: We aim to bring NASA's scientific knowledge closer to those who work the land through a web platform integrated with an intuitive and accessible conversational assistant . Our system evaluates weather conditions and soil health to anticipate potential crop risks, removing technological barriers so farmers of all ages—from young growers to older adults—can naturally consult and receive tailored guidance on what to plant and how to respond to climate challenges.
summary:
AgroVisions is a digital agricultural resilience platform that integrates NASA satellite data, local environmental measurements, and farmer-provided information to support informed agricultural decision-making.
The project combines an ESP32-based monitoring station with a DHT11 sensor to collect local temperature and relative humidity data. This information is integrated with satellite observations, including SMAP soil moisture, GPM IMERG precipitation estimates, and MODIS vegetation indices and land surface temperature. A web platform centralizes and visualizes these data, while an interactive chatbot allows farmers to access relevant information, alerts, and practical recommendations through simple natural-language queries and WhatsApp.
AgroVisions addresses the challenge of making complex Earth observation data understandable and accessible to agricultural producers, particularly those in rural communities with limited access to technology. By transforming scientific information into practical guidance, the project aims to help farmers anticipate climate-related risks, manage their crops more effectively, and strengthen agricultural resilience. Ultimately, AgroVisions seeks to contribute to climate change adaptation, sustainable agriculture, and food security.
details:
Problem Statement

Farmers are facing increasing vulnerability to extreme weather events, soil degradation, droughts, heavy rainfall, and unpredictable changes in agricultural patterns.

Although satellite monitoring and weather forecasting platforms are available, most require specialized technical knowledge or expensive equipment. This creates a technological gap that leaves thousands of farmers behind, even though they depend on timely and accurate decisions to protect their crops and ensure food security.

In this context, strengthening agricultural resilience requires not only generating information but also ensuring that it reaches those who need it, at the right time and through accessible channels.

This proposal emerged from the following research question:

How can the integration of satellite data and local measurements into a digital platform improve the availability and accessibility of information for farmers?

Although the availability of open satellite data has revolutionized our ability to monitor the Earth's surface, a significant gap remains between the generation of information and its effective delivery to farmers.

Earth observation data makes it possible to identify various environmental conditions that affect crops. However, this information often remains within technical platforms or specialized systems that are not always accessible to agricultural producers.

In response to this challenge, the team set out to transform satellite, observational, and locally collected data into clear, timely, and accessible alerts that farmers can understand and use to make informed agricultural decisions.

Figure 1. Project AgroVisions Logo

How does AgroVisions work?

AgroVisions works by integrating three main components: a web platform, an interactive chatbot, and local in-situ monitoring stations. Together, these components provide farmers with accessible agricultural and climate information to help them monitor crop conditions, identify potential risks, and make informed decisions.

1. In-situ Monitoring Stations

Local monitoring stations use an ESP32 microcontroller and a DHT11 sensor to collect environmental measurements, including ambient temperature and relative humidity. It is expected to add an NPK sensor to the station. This information complements satellite observations by providing measurements from the actual agricultural environment.

Figure 2. In-situ monitoring station (designed and built during the hackathon)

2. Web Platform

Check our platform

The web platform serves as the central hub for integrating and visualizing information from multiple sources, including NASA satellite data, local monitoring stations, and information provided directly by farmers. It presents relevant environmental conditions, alerts, and agricultural recommendations in an accessible format, helping users better understand the conditions affecting their crops.

It features a base map displaying the coordinates of the selected area of interest, the Soil Health Index (SHI), root-zone soil moisture, land surface temperature, 30-day accumulated rainfall, vegetation index, soil moisture dynamics, and water balance. It also includes an early warning system for environmental changes, a crop rotation recommendation engine, adjustable settings based on farmers’ priorities, and personalized, optimized adaptive crop rotation sequences.

Additionally, the platform provides indicators such as irrigation water savings, biological nitrogen contributions, water erosion control, and projected soil health. It also features a comparative simulator that evaluates conventional monoculture against adaptive crop rotation.

Alerts are displayed using a traffic-light system: green indicates favorable conditions, yellow signals caution, and red represents critical conditions. This system enables users to receive real-time notifications and make more informed decisions for better farm management.

Figure 3. Web Platform: Base MapFigure 4. Web Platform: Satellite-based diagnosis (humidity, temperature, rainfall, NDVI and SHI)Figure 5. Web Platform: Soil Moisture Dynamics and Water Balance GraphicsFigure 6. Web Platform: Early Warning SystemFigure 7. Web Platform: Crop Rotation SuggestionsFigure 8. Web Platform: Environmental and Economic BenefitsFigure 9. Web Platform: Comparison of single-crop farming vs. crop rotation

3. Interactive Chatbot

The chatbot provides a simple and user-friendly way for farmers to interact with AgroVisions. Through natural-language questions and commands, farmers can request information about their crops, access relevant environmental data, and receive contextualized alerts and recommendations. By connecting to the web platform, the chatbot makes complex agricultural and satellite information easier to understand and use.

Figure 10. WhatsApp Interactive Chatbot: Welcome conversation

Figure 11. WhatsApp Interactive Chatbot: Interaction

How the components work together?

The monitoring stations collect local environmental data, while satellite observations provide broader information about agricultural and environmental conditions. Farmer-provided information adds context about their crops and specific needs. These data sources are brought together on the web platform, where relevant information is organized and presented to support agricultural decision-making.

Farmers can then access this information through the web platform or interact with the chatbot using simple messages, including through WhatsApp. This integration transforms complex scientific and environmental data into accessible, practical information that helps farmers anticipate potential threats and manage their crops more effectively.

AgroVisions connects satellite technology, local monitoring, and human-centered interaction to put agricultural intelligence at farmers’ fingertips.

Benefits

The objective of AgroVisions is to democratize access to agricultural and climate information, strengthening farmers’ ability to anticipate risks and make informed decisions.

AgroVisions is more than just a dashboard. Its distinguishing value lies in transforming complex data into practical alerts and guidance for farmers through simple conversations with a chatbot.

Our tool is designed to be intuitive and easy for farmers to use. Users can submit their questions through voice commands or by navigating a simple, user-friendly menu.

Information from NASA satellite data, in-situ monitoring stations, and farmer-provided data is centralized on a single platform. Through a simple WhatsApp message, farmers can access this information and ask questions in an accessible and user-friendly environment.

AgroVisions puts precision agriculture at farmers’ fingertips, becoming their trusted ally and providing ongoing support for the important work they do.

Project Impact

According to a report by the University of Costa Rica, the area of cultivated land in the country decreased by between 10% and 27% between 2021 and 2024. This decline poses significant challenges to national agricultural production and food security.

In this context, it is not enough to recognize the importance of preserving agricultural land; it is also essential to strengthen farmers’ ability to make better use of their resources, anticipate climate-related threats, and make timely decisions regarding their crops.

AgroVisions aims to generate a positive impact on agricultural resilience, food security, and climate change adaptation by democratizing access to agricultural and climate information.

Its main impact lies in bridging the gap between the availability of scientific data and its practical use by farmers, particularly those living in rural communities with limited access to technology and connectivity.

By integrating NASA satellite data, measurements from local monitoring stations, and information provided by farmers themselves, AgroVisions facilitates the early identification of conditions that could threaten crops, such as droughts, heavy rainfall, excessive moisture, and water stress. This makes AgroVisions a trusted ally for farmers throughout every stage of the crop production process.

Furthermore, through easy-to-understand alerts, recommendations, and an interactive chatbot, the platform aims to strengthen farmers’ ability to anticipate potential risks and make evidence-based agricultural decisions.

In the long term, this initiative has the potential to help reduce crop vulnerability to extreme weather events, promote more efficient water resource management, facilitate agricultural planning and management, strengthen the adaptive capacity of farming communities, and contribute to food security and more sustainable agriculture.

Resources used

Hardware

  • ESP32 microcontroller for local environmental data acquisition.
  • DHT11 sensor for ambient temperature and relative humidity measurements.
  • 3D Printing with white PLA filament for the case.

Satellite and Environmental Data Sources

  • NASA SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive) for soil moisture information.
  • NASA GPM IMERG (Global Precipitation Measurement) for precipitation estimates.
  • MODIS Terra for vegetation indices (NDVI) and land surface temperature (LST).
  • NASA MERRA-2 for atmospheric reanalysis and meteorological information.

Software and Digital Platforms

  • AgroVisions web platform for data integration, visualization, alerts, and agricultural recommendations, developed in Javascript and Netlify.
  • Interactive chatbot for natural-language queries and farmer assistance.
  • WhatsApp for accessible communication and interaction with farmers.
  • NASA Earthdata as a source of Earth observation datasets.

How is AgroVisions creative?

The creativity of AgroVisions lies primarily in incorporating a chatbot as the interaction interface between farmers and the platform's satellite and agricultural data analysis system.

Traditionally, accessing Earth observation data requires navigating specialized platforms, interpreting maps, understanding technical indicators, and analyzing information from different sources. These requirements can create barriers for farmers who lack specialized technological knowledge.

AgroVisions proposes transforming this experience through a chatbot that allows farmers to interact with the platform in a simple, intuitive, and user-friendly way, using commands and natural-language queries. Instead of searching and interpreting information across different tools on their own, farmers can ask questions related to their crops and receive contextualized answers based on the data available in the system.

The chatbot connects to the web platform, where local measurements, satellite data, and information provided by farmers are integrated and displayed. In this way, it acts as an assistant that makes it easier to check environmental conditions, identify potential threats, and access agricultural alerts and recommendations.

This creative approach simplifies farmers’ interaction with technology, democratizes access to knowledge, makes technology more human-centered, supports timely decision-making, and integrates information from multiple sources.

AgroVisions' innovation is not simply about using satellite technology, but about making this technology more approachable, understandable, and accessible to those who need it most. Farmers do not have to learn how to interpret complex satellite systems because AgroVisions aims to bring that information directly to them through a simple conversation.

Factors considered

During the design of AgroVisions, the team considered technological, environmental, social, and accessibility factors to ensure that the solution addresses the real conditions of the agricultural sector.

Environmental and Agricultural Factors

  • Climate variability and the increasing frequency of extreme weather events.
  • Soil moisture conditions.
  • The specific characteristics and needs of different crops.
  • Changes in vegetation and potential crop stress conditions.
  • The importance of prevention and adaptation to environmental risks.

Technological Factors

  • Availability of open and up-to-date satellite data.
  • Integration of information from different sources, such as Ministerio de Agricultura y Ganadería (MAG), Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía (MINAE), Instituto Interamericano de Cooperación para la Agricultura (IICA), Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (INTA) and fertilizer companies.
  • Possibility of incorporating local sensors to complement satellite observations.
  • Ease of use of the platform and chatbot.
  • Availability of connectivity and functionality in rural communities.
  • Lack of satellites that directly measure NPK (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium).

Social and Economic Factors

  • Differences in farmers’ technological knowledge and skills.
  • Limited access to specialized devices and tools.
  • Need for affordable and easy-to-implement solutions.
  • Importance of providing information that is understandable and relevant to agricultural activities.
  • Farmers’ participation as a source of knowledge and as key decision-makers.

Together, these factors helped guide AgroVisions toward a solution that not only takes advantage of the capabilities of satellite observation but also considers the limitations, needs, and knowledge of the people who work directly in the field.
